content: No person has the power to have everything they want, but it is in their power not to want what they don't have.
author: Seneca
story:
Having survived eight years of political exile on the barren island of Corsica and the volatile, lethal court of Emperor Nero, Seneca understood the fragility of fortune and the necessity of philosophical armor. Writing to his companion Lucilius, he urged immediate, courageous living over anxious anticipation of future disasters.

In formulating this reflection, Seneca stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of desire. For Seneca, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
